A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioDiscoveryAgent, with matching core methods, datasets, and retained results. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the relocated agent trace.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrospective experiment-design simulations, including single-gene and two-gene evaluations, baseline comparisons, and tool and prompt ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original evaluations and adds comparator results, longer-run experiments, and measurements of token usage and API costs.

M1.justification: The core agent, prompts, tools, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 5 adds the limited Sonnet+Coreset procedural variant, which initializes Coreset using BioDiscoveryAgent's first-round predictions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six single-gene benchmarks and Horlbeck two-gene task. Changing 'five' to 'six' in Section 4.1 corrects the dataset count; longer runs and different batch sizes remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds two targeted comparators: the pathway/enrichment-based 'Human' baseline described in Appendix E and Sonnet+Coreset. Original comparators remain, and the hybrid also participates in the new longer-run comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 supplements the retained five-round comparisons with extensive 30-round evaluations using batches of 32 or 128 and non-essential-gene hit ratios (Tables 12–15). V2's existing 30-round prompt ablations are retained. The new comparisons substantially extend experimental budgets and controls; Scharenberg baselines cannot proceed beyond 24 rounds.

E4.justification: V3 adds substantial tests of persistence across experimental horizons and batch sizes, plus an initialization control testing whether agent predictions improve Coreset. Figure 9 and Tables 12–15 supplement the retained prompt/tool ablations. Appendix F additionally examines tool-use costs.

E5.justification: New Figure 9 specifies five-run averages with one-standard-deviation bands, while Tables 12–15 specify ten-run averages and display uncertainty at the final reported checkpoints. Existing results retain their run counts and uncertainty reporting; these additions do not establish increased replication of retained experiments.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds human/hybrid scores, model rankings, resource measurements, and extensive longer-run results. These are new conditions, not same-setting improvements over v2. Results are mixed: Table 12 reports Schmidt1 round-30 hit ratios of 0.293 for Sonnet, 0.303 for Coreset, and 0.314 for their hybrid at batch size 128.

T1.justification: The single-gene and two-gene formulations and hit-ratio equations remain unchanged. Section 2's added explanation of cumulative hits clarifies existing mathematics; no new formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions and claims, including 21% and 46% improvements, combinatorial performance exceeding twice the random baseline, and interpretability. The added evaluations do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds practical tool-use recommendations in Appendix D.1, a prediction-confidence hypothesis for differing tool benefits, and interpretations of hybrid performance. Appendix F attributes modest Haiku tool costs to fewer interaction turns. Existing limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 documents the Human baseline's initialization and enrichment procedure, including pathway identifiers in Table 6, and describes hybrid initialization. Table 11 adds actual input-token counts and per-trial API costs. Existing prompts, implementation descriptions, and code/data access provisions remain.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds limited discussion connecting the critic to reinforcement learning from AI feedback and agents' verbal reflection. The bibliography and central research positioning remain unchanged. New citation placeholders render as question marks, preventing identification of all discussed works.

P1.justification: V3 condenses tool descriptions, clarifies cumulative hit ratios and dataset counting, and updates front matter and disclosures. It adds Appendix D.1 and a computational-cost section, shifting the complete trace from F to G. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the experimental displays with pathway, ranking, cost, and longer-horizon tables (Tables 6, 8, and 11–15) and Figure 9. Table 1 gains comparator rows and Table 3 gains explanatory labels. Existing displays are retained, with appendix relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens v2's mainly five-round baseline evaluation through longer-horizon tests and an agent-initialized Coreset control, while actual cost reporting improves practical transparency. Reporting problems limit the gain: the broad hybrid interpretation needs qualification given Table 12's counterexamples, and new citations remain unresolved. The added controls and documentation nevertheless provide a modest net improvement.
